newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda, Ford seeking platform-sharing pact soon.
newsitem.headline: Mazda, Ford seeking platform-sharing pact soon.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp said on Thursday it is considering sharing car platforms with Ford Motor Co and it wants to make a decision by the end of March.
"We have plans to synchronise our cycle for launching new cars with that of Ford and to use common platforms. We are now studying the details of possible standardisation," a Mazda spokesman said.
Mazda is 33.3 percent owned by Ford.
Issues under consideration include which models should share standardised platforms and whether or not the move should include standardisation of power trains, including engines, he said.
The planned standardisation is part of Mazda's efforts to improve business efficiency, the spokesman said.
A car platform comprises a chassis and suspension. A power train is made up of an engine and transmission.
Japan's Jiji news agency reported on Thursday that under the standardisation plan, Mazda and Ford could use one million standardised engines per year.
The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun also reported on Thursday that Mazda and Ford had already agreed to share engines in the hope of cutting development costs.

Under the scheme, Mazda would develop engines for small vehicles and Ford would do the same for larger cars, the paper said. Mazda would develop an in-line four-cylinder model with a displacement of 1800-2000cc as the first engine to be developed under the scheme, the paper said.
